text.p: PRAVDA - The National Bank of Slovakia said the government did not accept the central banks' attitude to the prepared law on the revitalisation of the entrepreneurial sector, adding that it hoped parliament would amend the law from the original government draft.

- The paper quotes an unnamed official from junior coalition member, the Workers Party (ZRS), as saying the party would support bank privatisation under some certain instances, but that it would first demand deep control in the banks.

NARODNA OBRODA - State-run Slovak Railways (ZRS) has won a $200 million contract to build a 350 kilometre railway route in Guinea. It is ZRS's first commercial activity abroad. Construction work should begin in 1998 and last two years.
- The government should discuss a recovery programme for troubled state-owned white goods producer Calex at its regular session next Tuesday.

- The Bratislava Stock Exchange posted record turnover of 17.1 billion crowns in February 1997, some seven billion crowns more than in the previous month. Direct trades accounted for about 16 billion crowns.
- Car parts producer AVC said it would soon start producing gear boxes for the French car maker Peugeot, which shoud increase its turnover to 803 million crowns this year from 631 million in 1996.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak engineering sector accounted for about 50 billion crowns of the country's 1996 foreign trade balance.
SME - A NATO official said that if Slovakia would like to join the military alliance, there should be a positive outcome in a referendum on the subject.
